Alex — thanks, received the CSV and reviewed the patterns. High-level recommendation below (quick read):

1) Primary recommendation: H100-heavy reserved pool for latency-sensitive tails
   - Why: H100 provides best sustained FP16/TF32 throughput and typically delivers the lowest p95/p99 for generative workloads at 8k context. For your 512-token generation SLOs and 25 concurrent sessions, reserve 4 x H100 cards to start (we estimate this supports ~45 sustained QPS with conservative batching and prefix caching).
   - Memory: H100 supports the larger activation memory you need if you later move to 70B or add longer context.

2) Secondary node class: A100 as mid-tier for batch-heavy/off-peak work
   - Why: A100 is still strong for memory-bound configs and is more cost-efficient than H100 for background/throughput workloads. Keep 6 x A100 for daytime batch spikes and reranking jobs.

3) Cost-optimized option: L4 for lightweight routing / short-context requests
   - Why: L4 is a good fit for short context, small models, and embeddings/encoder tasks. Use L4 nodes for pre- and post-processing, and any shallow responses routing. Not recommended for your main 512-token generation path for p95-sensitive traffic.

Operational notes and levers:
- Caching: Enable prefix KV cache for interactive sessions — this can reduce effective work by ~20-40% depending on re-use.
- Batching policy: We recommend dynamic batching with a 30ms collect window to balance latency/throughput.
- Quantization: If you can tolerate small quality variance, int8/4-bit quantization reduces memory footprint and increases packing density (more instances per card).
- Autoscaling: Keep a small headroom (10-15% excess capacity) for warm-up to avoid cold misses.

Attachments: sku_lookup_sheet.xlsx (breakdown of instance performance curves and cost estimates).

If you'd like, we can map these to a 12-month reserved profile + burst hours and send a cost/latency projection.

Best,
Kimberly Park
